subject.title: fix(infra): bound stalled provider JSON/text/binary response reads with default chunk timeout

question: Should these generic exported response helpers impose 30-second JSON/text and 10-second error-body idle defaults even when callers or provider configuration select longer request deadlines?
rationale: The values change runtime semantics across a broad public helper surface; code inspection can verify the mechanism, but only maintainers can choose whether a hidden helper ceiling or caller-derived deadline is the intended compatibility contract.

options.title: Use caller-derived deadlines
options.body: Keep the additive options but derive idle budgets from the existing provider or operation timeout contract so generic helpers do not silently shorten configured requests.

options.title: Accept global safety defaults
options.body: Land the 30-second/10-second defaults after direct exported-helper proof and explicitly accept that they can terminate responses before a longer outer deadline.

recommendation.title: Use caller-derived deadlines
recommendation.body: Keep the additive options but derive idle budgets from the existing provider or operation timeout contract so generic helpers do not silently shorten configured requests.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed and merged the underlying chunk-timeout behavior and are the strongest available routing candidate for its broader default policy.
